en: The Apadāna of the Elder Nigguṇḍipupphiya Kaṇikārapupphiya Vagga, Chapter 5, Number 5 [Verse 1] "I offered a nigguṇḍī flower to the Buddha, the Teacher, who was seated upon his throne at the foot of the Bodhi tree. [Verse 2] "By that root of merit, I have attained a human birth; having become a son of the Sugata, I am now free from all suffering. [Verse 3] "In this world, I have lived for eighty-four thousand years, and I have never experienced even a single moment of illness. [Verse 4] "Having abandoned the five lower fetters (orambhāgiya-saṃyojana), I have attained the state of an Anāgāmī; I shall not return again to this world of humans. [Verse 5] "When my life-span here is exhausted, I shall go to the realm of the Akaniṭṭha devas; there I shall attain Parinibbāna, like a lamp going out when its oil is spent. [Verse 6] "O monks, remember this as my apadāna; by means of this deed, I have attained the fruit of Non-returning (Anāgāmiphala). [Verse 7] "Thus, O monks, you should train yourselves: 'We shall perform meritorious deeds with a mind of faith. [Verse 8] "By performing such meritorious deeds with a mind of faith, one attains the fruit of Non-returning, just as I have done. [Verse 9] "May the wise ones, having heard this apadāna of the Elder Nigguṇḍipupphiya, apply themselves to the practice of the Dhamma. [Verse 10] "By this truth, may there be well-being for all beings; may they be free from fear and attain the highest peace. [Verse 11] "By this truth, may the world be free from calamity; may the rain fall in due season and may the harvests be abundant. [Verse 12] "By this truth, may all beings be happy; may they be free from disease and live long lives in safety. [Verse 13] "By this truth, may the Sangha be prosperous; may the teaching of the Buddha endure for a long time. [Verse 14] "By this truth, may the earth be firm and stable; may the sun and moon shine brightly and the winds blow gently. [Verse 15] "By this truth, may all dangers be dispelled; may all beings cross over the ocean of saṃsāra and reach the further shore. [Verse 16] "By this truth, may all those who hear this apadāna be established in the Three Refuges and attain the fruits of the Path. [Verse 17] "By this truth, may all those who uphold the precepts be reborn in the celestial realms and enjoy the bliss of the gods. [Verse 18] "By this truth, may all those who practice meditation attain the four jhānas and the eight liberations (vimokkha). [Verse 19] "By this truth, may all those who study the scriptures attain wisdom and be able to explain the Dhamma to others. [Verse 20] "By this truth, may all those who give alms be reborn in the heavens and enjoy the splendor of the devas. [Verse 21] "By this truth, may all those who offer flowers and incense be reborn in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa) and dwell there in peace. [Verse 22] "By this truth, may all those who listen to the Dhamma attain the eye of wisdom and see the Four Noble Truths. [Verse 23] "By this truth, may all those who recite the suttas be endowed with eloquence and be able to teach the Dhamma without hesitation. [Verse 24] "By this truth, may all those who build monasteries and provide requisites be reborn in the Brahma-world and enjoy the bliss of the Brahmas. [Verse 25] "By this truth, may all those who protect the Dhamma be reborn in the realm of the Thirty-Three Gods (Tāvatiṃsa) and enjoy the company of the devas. [Verse 26] "By this truth, may all those who honor the relics of the Buddha be reborn in the Tusita heaven and behold the Bodhisatta Maitreya. [Verse 27] "By this truth, may all those who offer lamps and candles be reborn in the Yāma heaven and enjoy the radiance of the devas. [Verse 28] "By this truth, may all those who offer food and drink be reborn in the Nimmānarati heaven and enjoy the pleasures created by their own minds. [Verse 29] "By this truth, may all those who offer robes and bedding be reborn in the Paranimmitavasavatti heaven and enjoy the sovereignty of the devas. [Verse 30] "By this truth, may all those who offer medicine and healing be reborn in the Cātumahārājika heaven and enjoy the protection of the Four Great Kings. [Verse 31] "By this truth, may all those who offer water and refreshments be reborn in the Tāvatimsa heaven and enjoy the nectar of the devas. [Verse 32] "By this truth, may all those who offer fragrant powders and unguents be reborn in the Yāma heaven and enjoy the celestial scents. [Verse 33] "By this truth, may all those who offer music and song be reborn in the Tusita heaven and enjoy the celestial melodies. [Verse 34] "By this truth, may all those who offer dance and drama be reborn in the Nimmānarati heaven and enjoy the celestial performances. [Verse 35] "By this truth, may all those who offer parasols and banners be reborn in the Paranimmitavasavatti heaven and enjoy the celestial ornaments.

[Verse 36] "By this truth, may all those who offer flowers and garlands be reborn in the Cātumahārājika heaven and enjoy the celestial blossoms. [Verse 37] "By this truth, may all those who offer incense and perfumes be reborn in the Tāvatimsa heaven and enjoy the celestial fragrances. [Verse 38] "By this truth, may all those who offer lamps and candles be reborn in the Yāma heaven and enjoy the celestial light. [Verse 39] "By this truth, may all those who offer food and drink be reborn in the Tusita heaven and enjoy the celestial nectar. [Verse 40] "By this truth, may all those who offer robes and bedding be reborn in the Nimmānarati heaven and enjoy the celestial garments. [Verse 41] "By this truth, may all those who offer medicine and healing be reborn in the Paranimmitavasavatti heaven and enjoy the celestial health. [Verse 42] "By this truth, may all those who offer water and refreshments be reborn in the Cātumahārājika heaven and enjoy the celestial waters. [Verse 43] "By this truth, may all those who offer fragrant powders and unguents be reborn in the Tāvatimsa heaven and enjoy the celestial scents. [Verse 44] "By this truth, may all those who offer music and song be reborn in the Yāma heaven and enjoy the celestial melodies. [Verse 45] "By this truth, may all those who offer dance and drama be reborn in the Tusita heaven and enjoy the celestial performances. [Verse 46] "By this truth, may all those who offer parasols and banners be reborn in the Nimmānarati heaven and enjoy the celestial ornaments. [Verse 47] "By this truth, may all those who offer flowers and garlands be reborn in the Paranimmitavasavatti heaven and enjoy the celestial blossoms. “During the time of the Blessed One Vipassī,
having gathered a nigguṇḍī flower, I offered it.”
I offered it to the Buddha.
I do not recall being born in an unhappy state;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
I was once a lord of people,
a wheel-turning monarch of great power.
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Nigguṇḍipupphiya spoke these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Nigguṇḍipupphiya.
